title: Mate with king and rook

D0.outcome: Says that a king and a rook can force checkmate against a lone king, and that a rook alone cannot.

D1.outcome: Gives checkmate in one with king and rook against the lone king, on the edge of the board.

D2.outcome: Finds mate in two with king and rook, using a waiting move or a cut-off, without stalemating and without leaving the rook to be captured.

D3.outcome: Mates from a given starting position within the move budget against an engine opponent, without stalemate and without losing the rook.

misconceptions: The rook alone is enough to give mate.
A rook placed next to the enemy king is safe.
conditions: King and rook force mate on the edge: the rook cuts the king off, the own king comes up, and the last check is given along the edge.
Keep the rook safe: next to the enemy king it needs the support of your own king.
contrasts: A rook placed next to the enemy king without support is captured.
Which edge the mate happens on does not matter, only that it is an edge.
